title: Blocks
summary: A page's content is a list of typed blocks; each type is its own item here.
description: Blocks are the unit of content, storage and sync. New block types will be added over time, each as an item in this folder with its own prefix.

stories.as: the author of a book whose content will need new forms
stories.want: to add kinds of blocks over time
stories.soThat: the book's form can grow with what I write about

requirements.text: A page's content is an ordered list of blocks, not a Markdown text.

history.text: A note's content is an ordered list of blocks, not a Markdown text.
history.reason: The book is organised as a tree of pages instead of a flat set of notes.

requirements.text: Each block is its own database row.
Every block has exactly one type.
Adding a block type needs no change to how blocks are stored or synced.
A device that doesn't know a block's type shows it as a placeholder and leaves it unchanged.
Markdown syntax typed in the editor becomes the matching blocks.

history.reason: Content is stored as blocks, not Markdown text; Markdown remains the way the author writes.

requirements.text: Inline LaTeX in a block's text is rendered as typeset maths.

history.text: Inline LaTeX in a note is rendered as typeset maths.
history.reason: The book is organised as a tree of pages instead of a flat set of notes. Text lives in blocks.

requirements.text: The author can drag a block to another place in its page or into another page.
On a phone, a block is dragged by its handle with a finger, the page scrolling when the finger nears its top or bottom.
On a phone, a block's add button and handle stack vertically in a narrow margin, so its text keeps the screen's width.

Blocks stand `blocks.space` apart, beyond their lines' own spacing, so one paragraph visibly ends before the next. The items of a list stand together, with everything nested in them, and a list as a whole stands apart from what's around it as a paragraph does.

values.description: The room between blocks, beyond their lines' own: about half a line of the text.
